document.title: Cable from Secretary of State to Amembassy New Delhi: "Subject: Armacost Pre-summit Discussions with Vorontsov on Afghanistan"
document.authors: Secretary of State to U.S. Embassy New Delhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Contentious Armacost-Vorontsov discussion before the Reagan-Gorbachev summit on bringing positions closer on Afghanistan and a withdrawal timeframe. Vorontsov accepts Zahir Shah presiding over a loya jirga, criticizes Peshawar leaders, and reads an intelligence report alleging the U.S. ambassador met Hekmatyar, Sayyaf and Rabbani on Oct 21 to undermine national reconciliation.

events.description: Armacost and Vorontsov dinner discussion on Afghanistan.
Armacost-Vorontsov morning session on Afghanistan, Iran-Iraq war and southern Africa.
Soviet-alleged meeting of US Ambassador in Pakistan with Hekmatyar, Sayyaf and Rabbani and Pakistani officers (US denied the report).
Planned Vorontsov visit to Islamabad to test timetable proposal.
Armacost and Vorontsov dined and discussed Afghanistan, agreeing on points about withdrawal timetable and interim government.
Morning session of Armacost–Vorontsov talks on Afghanistan, Iran-Iraq war and southern Africa.
Vorontsov indicated a timetable for Soviet withdrawal would emerge from a final Geneva round in early 1988.
Planned Vorontsov visit to Islamabad in mid-December to discuss timetable and interim government.
Geneva cable 12223 sent to State reporting the Armacost-Vorontsov discussions.
Armacost pre-summit discussions with Vorontsov on Afghanistan: peacekeeping force, UN observers, troop withdrawal timetable, interim government.
Vorontsov presents draft summit communique language on Afghanistan supporting Cordovez's efforts and a political settlement.
Next Geneva round, possibly in January rather than February, where Soviets would announce a withdrawal timetable.
Soviet/Kabul July offer of portfolios to opposition, described as an opening bid with no follow-up.
PDPA party conference concluded, agreeing to describe itself as one party among many; planned Loya Jirga in November to approve a new constitution.
Soviet-alleged meeting of US ambassador in Pakistan with Hekmatyar, Sayyaf, Rabbani, and Pakistani military/government officials, disputed by Armacost.
Armacost pre-summit discussion with Vorontsov on Afghanistan: reconciliation, timetable for Soviet withdrawal, Cordovez's role, Loya Jirga.
Soviet/Kabul July offer of portfolios to the opposition, described as an opening bid with no follow-up.

relationships.quote: THE CONVOCATION OF A LOYA JIRGA UNDER THE AEGIS OF THE KING WOULD BE THE KEY EVENT.

sources_cited: Soviet oral report of 21 Oct 1987 meeting
key_claims: Soviets said a withdrawal timetable would be announced at the next Geneva round in early 1988, possibly January.
Vorontsov and Armacost agreed Zahir Shah could convene a Loya Jirga, preferably inside Afghanistan near the border rather than Islamabad.
Armacost argued the new DRA constitution consolidates Najib's and PDPA power and hinders reconciliation; Vorontsov called it transitional.
Vorontsov claimed the US ambassador in Pakistan met Hekmatyar, Sayyaf and Rabbani on 21 Oct 1987 to plan Stinger deployments and US advisers; US officials called this misrepresentation.
Armacost stressed US would only act as Geneva guarantor if Soviet withdrawal was phased and front-loaded.
Both sides discussed an Austrian State Treaty-style neutrality model for Afghanistan and a possible UN observer or peacekeeping presence.
